title: Take out an interrupted suture: forceps lift the knot, a stitch cutter cuts flush, then draw it out toward the wound
instruction: Take out the stitch: lift the knot with the forceps, cut the leg away from the knot flush with the skin with the stitch cutter, draw the stitch out toward the wound, put it on the gauze and the instruments back in their trays, and take your hands away from the pad.
context: Medical assistants (O*NET 31-9092.00, about 811,000 US jobs) have the core task 'Help physicians examine and treat patients, handing them instruments or materials or performing such tasks as giving injections or removing sutures.' (O*NET, USDOL/ETA, CC BY 4.0; O*NET is a trademark of USDOL/ETA). Limbs & Things (named for identification only), a maker of suture practice pads, teaches the removal (limbsandthings.com/media/busponzi/suture-aftercare-manual.pdf): 'Grasp the knot with dissecting forceps, and then cut the suture precisely with scissors, flush with the tissue surface, so that the exposed length of suture (which may be contaminated) does not have to pass through the tissues', then 'Remove the suture by pulling back towards the wound so that the wound edges are not drawn apart'. UK and EU removal kits pair the forceps with a single-use stitch cutter, as here; US kits mostly pair them with small Littauer scissors, which make the same cut.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A silicone suture practice pad, 12 x 8 cm with 8 mm of skin on a 2.2 cm block, has its middle at (32, 0) and a 5 cm incision along x. One interrupted stitch crosses the incision, tied to this lab's standard: 3-0 monofilament nylon (about 0.25 mm), simple interrupted, a square knot of 3 throws (two flat throws and a third to lock), both tails cut to 5 mm, the knot snug to the skin on the +y side, each bite entering and leaving the skin 4 mm from the incision's edge (an 8 mm span). In the simulator the strand is one rigid curved piece on joints (not a thread): its lift, cut and draw are set by code. Dissecting forceps (12 cm, 12 g, tips 4 mm apart when open) stand tips-down in a slotted foam rest on a 16 x 9 cm steel tray (its long side along x) at (34, 16); a single-use stitch cutter (a 9 cm flat steel blade, 6 mm wide, 6 g, ending in a hooked notch 3.5 mm high over a 0.8 mm foot, its sharp inner edge 3 mm in) stands hook-down in a foam rest on its own tray at (30, -15). A 7.5 cm gauze square lies at (24, 20), its corner over the forceps tray's. The arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Cumulative, on outcomes a camera or a person can check, all in whole millimetres or yes/no. 0.25: the knot caught in the forceps (tips within 3 mm of it) and lifted at least 2 mm (side camera, mm scale). 0.5: also the far leg (away from the knot) cut, with no more than 2 mm of it left standing above the skin (the cutter's hook slid in level under the lifted stitch, from beside it, never down through it; yes/no on the drawn-out stitch, mm scale). Both legs cut: 0.5 at most. 0.75: also the stitch drawn out of the skin by the knot: the forceps' tips 12 mm from where the knot lay and at least 3 mm toward the wound (-y), the wound's gap under 3 mm throughout (top camera, mm scale). 1.0: also the stitch let go on the gauze, both instruments let go and resting in their trays, off the gauze, every fingertip of both hands 4 cm outside the pad block's outline, held 2 s (top and wrist cameras). 0 at any time: the knot pulled 5 mm up before the cut (torn through the skin), or the cutter pressed more than 2 mm into the silicone (pad checked for a cut afterwards).
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz. The stitch is one rigid curved strand on joints, not a thread: a soft-body thread 0.25 mm thick is not modelled (it would need far smaller steps, and lift, cut and draw must be read exactly). It is drawn 0.6 mm thick, no collider; code sets its lift, cut and draw from the forceps' tips and the cutter's notch. Forceps hinge is sprung. Approximated: tear and dig limits, the gap's stiffness.
scores: Dream-1 run (revised task): no score (the provider's API refused the first inference request, before the policy acted: 'unsafe instruction, refused: Cutting stitches on skin risks sharp instrument contact and harm to people.'); demo: 1.0
reset_notes: One fixed layout; no seed changes the scene. On a real trial, a fresh 3-0 nylon stitch is tied for each trial across the incision's middle (the lab's standard: 3-0 nylon, simple interrupted, a square knot of 3 throws, 5 mm tails, 4 mm bites, snug to the skin, the knot on the +y side), ink-marked where it leaves the skin; the pad is replaced when its incision tears.
no_video_reason: The provider's API refused the first inference request before the policy acted: 'DreamAPI refused the inference request: DA-4000 BAD_REQUEST (malformed): unsafe instruction, refused: Cutting stitches on skin risks sharp instrument contact and harm to people.'
